The instance cards say what each instance is doing, and let you start it, stop it, or open it.

## ✨ Added

- **Every instance card carries its queue.** How many files are owed, how much is left, how fast it is moving, and whether the queue is paused. Read live through the relay, so it is the instance's own answer rather than a guess from the last time anything was sent to it.
- **Play and stop, per instance.** Two separate controls rather than one that changes meaning: a switch whose glyph flips is something you have to read before you dare press it, and this one sits in a list where the first question is "which instance was that again". Stopping halts the queue and lets what is already running finish, exactly like the same control in the app itself.
- **Open the interface**, in a new tab. The extension holds no addresses, so it asks the instance for its own — over the encrypted channel, never through the relay in the clear. An instance with no address to offer keeps the control, disabled, rather than hiding it: a button that appears on one card and not another reads as a fault in the card.
- **The cards are bigger** and the mark grew with them.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **"Take the look from the instance" locked the options and never unlocked them.** Switching it off left the colours, corners and rainbow greyed out and unclickable. The unlock read back the very value it was trying to clear, so once set it could never be cleared.
- **Switching it off now puts your own look back.** Adopting the instance's look overwrote the local one with nothing kept, so the switch was one-way in everything but appearance. What was there before is stashed on the way in and restored on the way out.
- **Rainbow mode only reached part of the extension.** Card headings had a palette position and nothing else did, so the mode was on while the buttons, switches and the popup went on wearing the single accent. Positions now sit on the containers, so everything inside a card follows it, and the popup and the send-to window have their own runs.

## 📋 Notes

- **One new route is readable by group members**: the addresses an instance answers on, which is what makes "open the interface" possible without the extension storing an address. It travels inside the encrypted frame, so the relay still learns nothing about where anybody's instance lives. Holding the connection phrase already means being able to drive that instance's queue and read its task list.
- The ten new interface strings are lifted verbatim from the app's own 42 locales rather than translated again, so both surfaces say the same words for the same things.
